pairs.subject: usage-event-ingestion
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/events.rs:43 The transmission id is optional: it is server-minted when absent (LlmEvent `#[serde(default = "crate::new_id")]`) or blank, so an emitter that leaves it out has no idempotence and a retried POST double-counts cost and cap usage. The technique explicitly refuses this.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/events.rs:43 The key is optional with a server-minted default, which the technique names as the failure. Duplicate handling is otherwise good: a replay with the same payload gets 200 duplicate:true, a different payload gets a terminal 409 (first write wins), and batch items are reported per item. But the replay read-back is project-scoped (events.rs:284) while the key is global, so a cross-project id collision is wrongly reported as 'already exists with a different payload'.

crates/api/src/events_validate.rs:184 The door refuses only payload-intrinsic or machinery-corrupting values: empty model, oversized trace ids, a usage sub-count above its total, and implausible ts skew. Configuration-dependent facts (unmodeled provider, unpriced model, unregistered use case) are admitted and surfaced later in bulk via GET /v1/costs/unpriced (costs_unpriced.rs).

crates/api/src/otlp/mod.rs:160 The OTLP door only maps spans and hands them to the native batch handler, and single and batch share prepare_event. There is one implementation of the admission contract, not two.

crates/api/src/otlp/mod.rs:7 Only per-call trace spans and events are ingested. There are no interval counter reports (OTLP metrics) and so no temporality to decode; grepping temporality/cumulative found nothing.
crates/api/src/events.rs:257 Events resolve to a project, not to a windowed subscription. Grepping 'subscription' over the ingest files found nothing.

pairs.registryProposal: thin-ingest-deferred-validation does not cover synchronous budget/limit admission, which by nature reads per-tenant rules and rolling usage at the door. It should say whether cap enforcement is an accepted exception to 'door cost must not scale with configuration'.
